papers.title: Climatic and Anthropogenic Drivers of Amphibian Richness and Vulnerability in Nigeria.
papers.abstract: Amphibians are the most threatened vertebrate group, yet broad-scale patterns of diversity, environmental sensitivity, and extinction risk remain poorly understood across tropical Africa. Nigeria supports high amphibian diversity at the interface of forest and savanna systems, but uneven survey coverage limits understanding of diversity patterns, environmental drivers, and climate risks. In this study, we assessed the patterns and drivers of amphibian species richness and species vulnerability, as well as the projected impacts of climate change on amphibians distributed across Nigeria. To do this, we analyzed 1110 spatially filtered occurrence records representing 119 species across the country. We combined multi-scale species richness analyses, boosted regression tree modeling, vulnerability assessments, climate projections for 25 sufficiently sampled species, and evaluations of projected changes in species richness inside and outside protected areas. Results showed that observed species richness was concentrated in southern forests and montane regions. However, more than 95% of grid cells lacked occurrence records, revealing substantial sampling gaps that limit robust inference at the national scale. Our study revealed the important role of Human Footprint Index in shaping amphibian species richness patterns in Nigeria. Results also showed that a subset of environmental variables such as isothermality, precipitation of the warmest quarter, the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index, mean diurnal range, and distance to the nearest river influenced the amphibian species richness patterns. Furthermore, 40 species (33.6%) were classified in the highest vulnerability category, particularly range-restricted taxa with narrow elevational ranges and high anthropogenic exposure. papers.title: Deciphering hepatocyte-HSC Jagged1-Notch crosstalk in MASH-induced liver fibrosis.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND & AIMS: Hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) are key drivers of fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). Hepatocyte expression of Jagged1, a critical Notch ligand, is increased in patients with MASH-associated fibrosis, and is necessary to induce fibrosis in mice, attributed to inter-hepatocyte Notch signaling. As HSC Notch activity is also increased in patients and mouse models of MASH, we investigated whether hepatocyte to HSC Notch signaling provides a parallel and additive path to liver fibrosis. METHODS: Longitudinal analysis of liver-related events and survival outcomes was conducted in patients with MASH. Genetic mouse models of HSC Notch loss- and gain-of-function were generated and characterized to determine the role of Notch signaling in MASH diet-induced liver fibrosis. Ligand-specific induction using tethered Jagged1 combined with γ-secretase inhibitor-mediated Notch inhibition, hepatocyte Jagged1 manipulation with or without HSC-specific Notch loss-of-function, pathway enrichment analysis from RNA sequencing of primary mouse HSCs induced by Jagged1, and snRNA-seq analysis were performed to identify underlying regulatory mechanisms. RESULTS: Increased HSC Notch activity was associated with a higher risk of liver-related events and all-cause mortality in patients with MASH, independent of fibrosis stage. Blocking HSC Notch activity reduced Jagged1-induced cellular activation in vitro, and ameliorated MASH diet-induced liver fibrosis, as well as hepatocyte Jagged1-induced HSC activity in mice, likely through interaction with Notch2. Conversely, forced HSC Notch activation exacerbated MASH diet-induced liver fibrosis by means of a fibrogenic program dependent on TGF-β signaling. CONCLUSIONS: These findings reveal a therapeutically tractable Jagged1-Notch signaling axis that regulates HSC activity in MASH-related liver fibrosis.

papers.title: A glucose-conjugated "turn-on" AIE probe for on-site sensing and long-term tracking of tumor cells.
papers.abstract: Fluorescent probes are revolutionizing bio-imaging and disease detection due to their ability to provide real-time, high-resolution imaging with minimal invasiveness. Their high sensitivity and photostability make them invaluable for tracking cellular processes, diagnosing diseases, and even monitoring treatment efficacy. Most fluorescent probes rely on UV radiation for excitation, which can lead to cell damage, photobleaching, and limited imaging depth, driving researchers to develop probes that can be excited by visible or near-infrared (NIR) light, which are less harmful to cells and tissues. The current reconnoiter, a glucose-coupled turn-on yellow, fluorescent probe, seems to be a promising tool for bio-imaging. Its design leverages unique properties such as a large Stokes shift and environmental sensitivity, combined with AIE characteristics to enhance fluorescence in aggregated states. This could make it highly effective for imaging HeLa cancer cells with improved sensitivity and reduced background interference. This work is focused on developing Glu-1-O-SHY, a new glucose-coupled turn-on ESIPT-based AIE yellow fluorescent probe for bio-imaging of HeLa cancer cells. The probe was synthesized by condensation of hydrazine with 1-O-Glu-4-(diethylamino)-benzaldehyde, followed by deacetylation. The probe was characterized, its AIE behavior was studied in THF/water mixtures, and its turn-on response was examined upon hydrolysis of the glucose unit. Cytotoxicity was assessed in HepG2, HeLa and Chang cells after 24 h, and live-cell imaging was performed in HeLa cells by confocal fluorescence microscopy with and without added glucose. The novelty of this work lies in combining, in a single molecule, a symmetrical hydrazone ESIPT/AIE fluorophore with a glucose unit at the anomeric 1-O position, coupling GLUT-1-mediated uptake with turn-on yellow emission; to the best of our knowledge, such a glucose-conjugated hydrazone AIE probe has not been reported before. papers.title: Loss of atypical chemokine receptor GPR182 drives MASLD-like liver fibrosis with neutrophilic infiltration and CXCL10 accumulation.
papers.abstract: Liver sinusoidal endothelial cells (LSECs) line the hepatic sinus of the liver and control organ function, immune cell infiltration, and liver fibrosis. We have demonstrated that the deletion of Gata4 and Maf in LSECs leads to endothelial dysfunction, which subsequently results in liver fibrosis. GPR182 is an atypical chemokine receptor that is strongly expressed in sinusoidal endothelial cells and whose expression is reduced in liver fibrosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. However, the functional role of GPR182 in LSEC homeostasis and liver fibrogenesis remains unclear. We used a global constitutive Gpr182 knockout mouse (designated Gpr182-KO) and analyzed livers histologically, as well as by immunofluorescent staining and qPCR. Mice were fed a choline-deficient, l-amino acid-defined (CDAA) diet to study metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) in Gpr182-KO mice. Hepatic infiltration of immune cells was analyzed using flow cytometry. Picrosirius red staining revealed a perisinusoidal liver fibrosis in Gpr182-KO mice. Hepatic stellate cell (HSC) markers COL1A1 and COL3A1 as well as Desmin and PDGFRB were significantly increased, while αSMA was unchanged, which is consistent with an increase in capillary-pericyte-like HSCs. The expression levels of LSEC markers LYVE-1 and STAB2 were significantly decreased, whereas continuous endothelial cell marker CD146 was significantly upregulated in Gpr182-KO mice. Diet-induced MASH aggravated GPR182-associated liver fibrosis. Gpr182-KO livers exhibited increased levels of the profibrotic chemokine CXCL10, indicating reduced GPR182-scavenging activity. An increased neutrophilic immune cell infiltration was observed in GPR182-KO livers. Our findings suggest that GPR182 controls the homeostasis of the hepatic niche and prevents liver fibrosis.

papers.title: Sexual dimorphism in weapons arises from amplification of shared developmental pathways.
papers.abstract: Sexually selected traits are expected to be especially sensitive to developmental condition, but the pathways generating sex differences in environmental sensitivity remain unclear. We manipulated juvenile nutrition and developmental group size in European earwigs (Forficula auricularia sensu lato) and fitted a combined-sex Bayesian structural equation model linking development time, body size, forceps length, and elytra length. Compared with the standard diet, the nutrient-diluted diet reduced forceps length in both sexes, with a substantially greater reduction in males through both direct and growth-mediated pathways. Rearing with 4 or 8 nymphs rather than 1 nymph also increased male forceps more strongly, primarily through direct, body-size-independent paths. These sex differences were much larger for forceps than for elytra, a nonweapon comparison trait. The pronotum-forceps relationship was markedly stronger in males, whereas treatment effects on pronotum length were broadly similar between sexes. Development time and forceps length were negatively correlated among maternal families in males; the corresponding female association was similar in direction but less precise. The same hypothesised developmental cascade was therefore consistent with both sexes, but male weapon expression showed stronger environmental responsiveness and greater amplification of body-size variation.

papers.title: Hepatic EPHX1 potentiates liver fibrosis by decreasing eicosatrienoic acids.
papers.abstract: Changes in polyunsaturated fatty acid metabolites are thought to contribute to pathogeneses of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and liver fibrosis. This study demonstrated that hepatic microsomal epoxide hydrolase (EPHX1) promotes liver fibrosis by decreasing hepatic eicosatrienoic acid (EET) levels, suggesting that elevation of serum dihydroxyeicosatrienoic acid (DHET) levels is an indicator of advanced fibrosis. Serum lipidomic analysis of 102 patients with MASLD and 121 with chronic hepatitis C, combined with multivariate logistic regression, confirmed elevation of serum 11,12-DHET levels as a predictor of advanced fibrosis. The expression of hepatic EPHX1, which hydrolyzes EET to DHET, increased in patients with advanced fibrosis. MASLD mouse model showed increased hepatic EPHX1 levels and decreased hepatic EET levels. Ephx1-null mice showed suppressed hepatic fibrogenesis and oxidative stress with increasing EET levels. In hepatic stellate cells (HSCs), treatment with 11,12-EET reduced COL1A1 expression, but not 11,12-DHET, attenuated intracellular oxidative stress, and suppressed TGF-β-induced HSC activation. Furthermore, it alleviated liver fibrosis by attenuating hepatic oxidative stress and suppressing HSC activation in mice with thioacetamide-induced liver fibrosis. This study provides evidence that EPHX1 contributes to EET hydrolysis in the liver and participates in liver fibrogenesis, suggesting its potential as a therapeutic target.

papers.title: Modelling Environmental Sensitivity of Sexual Precocity Indicator Traits in Nellore Cattle Using Genomic Reaction Norms.
papers.journal: Journal of animal breeding and genetics = Zeitschrift fur Tierzuchtung und Zuchtungsbiologie
papers.abstract: Sexual precocity indicator traits in Nellore cattle are key drivers of the profitability and sustainability of beef production. In tropical regions, environmental variability may affect the expression of reproductive traits, and failure to account for genotype-by-environment interaction (GxE) may compromise selection accuracy. In this context, we used genomic reaction norm models to investigate GxE for sexual precocity traits in Nellore cattle and to estimate genetic parameters and associations across environmental gradients (derived from contemporary group solutions for body weight adjusted to 455 days, an indicator of environmental quality). The sexual precocity indicator traits evaluated in this study were heifer early calving probability at 30 months (HC30), age at first calving (AFC), scrotal circumference at 365 days (SC365) and age at puberty in males (APM). The genetic expression of sexual precocity indicator traits was found to be influenced by EG levels, with heritabilities ranging from 0.12 to 0.68 for SC365, 0.13 to 0.55 for APM, 0.09 to 0.54 for AFC and 0.07 to 0.35 for HC30. Genetic correlations across EG levels for male and female sexual precocity traits were environment-dependent, with the magnitude and, in some cases, the direction of correlations varying across the EG. In particular, genetic associations between male indicator traits and female reproductive traits weakened under more favourable environmental conditions, suggesting reduced efficiency of indirect selection for female precocity under improved production systems. Plasticity classification, defined according to the absolute value of individual reaction norm slopes, revealed a predominance of robust individuals for APM (72.5%) and SC365 (47.2%), whereas AFC and HC30 showed greater proportions of plastic and highly plastic animals, with 65.4% and 64.3% of animals classified as plastic or highly plastic, respectively.
