papers.title: Engineered micro-nano system for ADSC-exosomes-based therapy of liver fibrosis via ROS elimination and PPARγ/PCK1 pathway reactivation.
papers.abstract: Liver fibrosis is a progressive hepatic disorder driven by persistent oxidative stress and dysregulated transcriptional reprogramming of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs). Effective clinical interventions remain extremely limited, as targeting a single pathological pathway provides only partial benefit and fails to fully arrest disease progression. Herein, by screening a dynamic human liver fibrosis organoid model, we identified miR-3682-3p as a previously unrecognized pro-fibrotic driver that was upregulated during fibrosis progression and associated with disease severity. To enable dual-pathway intervention, we engineered a targeted nanotherapeutic platform based on adipose-derived stem cell exosomes (ADSC-EVs), loaded with a miR-3682-3p inhibitor (in-3682) and surface-decorated with cRGDyk-modified cerium oxide (CeO) nanozymes. This platform, termed RC@EVs-in3682, preferentially targets activated HSCs and concurrently mitigates oxidative stress and pro-fibrotic signaling, thereby suppressing HSC activation, contraction, and migration. Moreover, in a carbon tetrachloride (CCl)-induced mouse model of liver fibrosis, RC@EVs-in3682 reduced collagen deposition and restored hepatic architecture. Mechanistically, our findings support that inhibition of miR-3682-3p and CeO-mediated ROS scavenging together promote the restoration of the peroxisome proliferator activated receptor γ (PPARγ)/PCK1 axis; accordingly, RC@EVs-in3682 restores PPARγ-dependent PCK1 expression and the associated metabolic program. Collectively, our study provides a multifunctional nanoplatform and establishes RC@EVs-in3682 as a promising nanotherapeutic strategy for liver fibrosis by simultaneously targeting oxidative stress and pro-fibrotic signaling.

papers.title: Foetal sex is a key determinant of pathogen-specific innate immune responses in amniotic fluid-derived cells.
papers.abstract: AIM: Foetal sex is increasingly recognized as a critical biological variable influencing immune development and susceptibility to intrauterine stressors, including infection. However, the mechanisms by which foetal sex modulates innate immune responses at the maternal-foetal interface remain poorly understood. METHODS: We investigated sex-dependent innate immune responses in human amniotic fluid-derived cells (AFCs) using an in vitro model of infection with two pre-term birth-related pathogens, Streptococcus agalactiae (GBS) and Escherichia coli. We evaluated gene and protein expression of key pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, TNF-α), Toll-like receptors (TLR2 and TLR4), and selected microRNAs (miRNAs), involved both in pro-inflammatory signalling pathways and negative regulators of inflammation. KEY FINDINGS: GBS infection induced a selective inflammatory response characterized by increased TNF-α production and TLR2 protein expression, with stronger responses observed in male AFCs. In contrast, female AFCs exhibited enhanced expression of regulatory miRNAs, including miR-29 family members, associated with reduced TNF-α levels. E. coli infection had a limited functional impact on the inflammatory parameters in our experimental conditions. Although it induced transcriptional activation of inflammatory genes, no significant changes were observed at the protein level. In female cells, E. coli infection was associated with increased expression of miR-146a-5p and miR-19a-3p, along with a reduction in miR-18a-5p. SIGNIFICANCE: Foetal sex is a key determinant of pathogen-specific innate immune responses in AFCs. This sex-dependent immune modulation may contribute to differential susceptibility to inflammation-driven pregnancy complications and highlights the importance of incorporating foetal sex as a biological variable in studies of intrauterine infection.

papers.title: Base Editing of Hematopoietic Stem Cells Corrects Gain-of-Function Mutations in APDS.
papers.abstract: Activated phosphoinositide 3-kinase delta syndrome 1 and 2 (APDS1, APDS2) are rare gain-of-function inborn errors of immunity (IEI) leading to recurrent severe infections, bronchiectasis, lymphoproliferation and lymphoma. APDS1 and APDS2 are caused by mutations in PIK3CD and PIK3R1 respectively, which together encode the subunits of the phosphoinositide 3-kinase  enzyme (PI3K). The only curative therapy is allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (alloHSCT), which requires a suitable donor and incurs a significant risk of morbidity and mortality. An adenine base editing strategy was developed to target the most frequent point mutations in APDS1 (p.E1021K, c.3061G>A; ~90% of patients) and APDS2 (c.1425+1G > A; ~50% of patients). Highly efficient correction of the pathogenic point mutation was achieved in patient T cells and hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) and associated with functional restoration of PI3K signaling, rescue of the activation-induced cell death phenotype and, in APDS2, abrogated expression of the pathogenic splice isoform. Edited HSCs maintained pluripotency and achieved long-term engraftment in immunodeficient mice. A healthy control:APDS1 mixed chimera mouse model suggested that 75% wild-type engraftment generated a wild-type phenotype with respect to T and B cell dysfunction and lymphoproliferation, and thus similar editing efficiencies would be predicted to improve patient clinical phenotype. Together, these data demonstrate successful application of base editing to a gain-of-function IEI, with potential for application in other diseases.

papers.title: Revisiting the role of fluorescent dyes in the detection of amorphous and amyloid aggregates: The quest continues.
papers.abstract: Protein aggregation is a hallmark of various neurodegenerative and systemic disorders, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and type 2 diabetes. The ability to detect and characterize aggregates in both in vitro and in vivo systems is crucial for understanding disease mechanisms and developing diagnostic strategies. Fluorescent dyes have emerged as powerful tools for probing protein aggregates, offering insights into their structural variations and formation pathways. This review provides a comprehensive comparison of classical and emerging fluorescent dyes. It correlates their binding specificity and performance metrics, including quantum yield, fluorescence enhancement, and binding affinity, with molecular recognition mechanisms such as TICT restriction, π-π stacking, hydrophobic interactions, and electrostatic interactions. We categorize the dyes based on their blood-brain barrier (BBB) crossing ability, positron emission tomography (PET) imaging suitability, environmental sensitivity, nucleic acid binding affinity, luminescent conjugated oligothiophenes (LCOs), and nanoparticle-conjugation. We also consider their applicability to in vitro, in vivo and ex vivo settings, highlighting their use in detecting different aggregate species. We further assess dye suitability for amyloid versus amorphous aggregates and for different experimental contexts, considering critical parameters. By bridging structural features with functional outcomes, this review offers guidance for probe selection and highlights future directions for rational dye design to enhance sensitivity and selectivity in aggregate detection.

papers.title: Efficacy and safety of romiplostim in refractory aplastic anaemia: a plain language summary of phase II/III, multicentre, open-label study.
Experimental Basis for Split Dose and Repeated Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation.
papers.abstract: In clinical hematopoietic cell transplantation, donor cells are typically administered as a single infusion shortly after myeloablative conditioning. The future availability of ex vivo expanded hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) products may make split-dose and repeated transplantation strategies feasible. The biological basis and therapeutic potential of split-dose and repeated hematopoietic cell transplantation remain poorly understood. We conducted a series of experiments in mice to evaluate split-dose, repeated, and delayed bone marrow transplantation (BMT) strategies. Repeated BMTs demonstrated that engraftment of HSCs from subsequent grafts is not impaired during early hematopoietic reconstitution and remains efficient after hematopoietic recovery. While transplantation of a single or repeated large cell doses reduced the engraftment of progenitor cells administered after four days, the engraftment of HSCs was not affected by previous transplantations. The reduced hematopoietic chimerism from delayed repeated BMT administered after recovery of blood production suggests partial HSC compartment reconstitution from the initial transplant. Repeated transplantation strategies may improve the stability of donor chimerism and long-term hematopoietic recovery. Multi-dose transplantation approaches may also prove valuable for gene-modified HSC-based therapies.

papers.title: Klotho Alleviates Liver Fibrosis by Modulating TGF-β-Integrin Signaling During Hepatic Stellate Cell Transdifferentiation.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) drive liver fibrosis through myofibroblastic transdifferentiation following liver injury. Transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β)/Smad signaling and integrin-dependent mechanisms are established regulators, but how these pathways interact during fibrogenesis remains incompletely defined. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: We examined integrin-mediated signaling in TGF-β-driven HSC transdifferentiation and evaluated the antifibrotic effects of α-Klotho. KEY RESULTS: Primary mouse HSCs underwent spontaneous fibrogenic transdifferentiation in vitro with increased integrin expression and integrin-associated FAK signaling. Acute TGF-β1 stimulation induced both Smad and FAK phosphorylation. Pharmacological and genetic inhibition of TGF-β receptors strongly suppressed Smad activation but had limited effects on the acute FAK response, whereas integrin αV knockdown selectively reduced FAK phosphorylation without altering Smad activation. Inhibition of either TGF-β receptor or integrins attenuated the longer-term fibrogenic response. Intracellular Ca²⁺ chelation suppressed both signaling arms and subsequent fibrogenic marker expression. Biochemical analyses supported an association between active TGF-β1 and integrin αV. Exogenous α-Klotho attenuated integrin-associated and TGF-β signaling and exerted additional antifibrotic effects beyond pharmacological integrin inhibition, whereas knockdown of endogenous α-Klotho enhanced fibrogenic signaling. In vivo, α-Klotho administration attenuated the development of thioacetamide-induced liver fibrosis, accompanied by reduced integrin/FAK and TGF-β/Smad signaling. CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: Integrin-associated signaling is a complementary component of the TGF-β-driven fibrogenic response in HSCs, involving crosstalk among TGF-β/Smad, integrin/FAK, and Ca²⁺ signaling. &#x

papers.title: Hepatic stellate cells remodel liver-resident CD8+ T cells and constrain immunosurveillance.
papers.abstract: The liver constitutes a distinct immunological niche in which CD8+ T cells balance immune protection and tissue integrity. How chronic liver disease (CLD) remodels human liver-resident CD8+ T cells remains poorly understood. We demonstrate that activated hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) create immunoinstructive fibrotic niches that regulate liver-resident CD8+ T cell differentiation, localization, and function. CD103-expressing liver-resident CD8+ T cells accumulate with increasing fibrosis severity and preferentially localize within collagen-rich scar tissue. HSC-derived and matrix-retained TGFβ promote acquisition of a residency program characterized by upregulation of CD103, ECM-binding integrins, and adhesion molecules. Despite their increased abundance, liver-resident CD8+ T cells in CLD exhibit impaired antigen-dependent effector function, increased inhibitory receptor expression, and a transcriptional program associated with T cell dysfunction. Importantly, responses to PMA/ionomycin remain intact, indicating preserved effector competence. Mechanistically, HSCs directly suppress antigen-specific liver-resident CD8+ T cell function, with partial restoration following PD-L1/PD-L2 blockade. These findings identify the fibrotic niche as a central regulator of liver-resident CD8+ T cells and reveal how fibrosis can limit local immunosurveillance.

papers.title: Feline intestinal organoids reveal cell type-specific tropism and antiviral responses to type II feline infectious peritonitis virus.
papers.abstract: Feline infectious peritonitis virus (FIPV), a highly pathogenic feline coronavirus (FCoV), causes a nearly uniformly fatal disease in cats, yet its infection dynamics within the intestinal epithelium-the primary site of viral entry and replication-remain largely unresolved. Here, we report the first establishment of long-term, passageable three-dimensional (3D) feline intestinal organoids, including feline ileal organoids (fILOs) and feline colonic organoids (fCOs), which faithfully recapitulate the cellular diversity and architecture of the feline intestine and support infection by type II FIPV. Using this physiologically relevant platform, we demonstrate that FIPV infection induces profound epithelial remodeling in fCOs, characterized by a marked expansion of proliferative cell populations and depletion of differentiated epithelial lineages. High-resolution single-cell RNA sequencing of fCOs revealed pronounced cell type-specific viral tropism, with preferential infection of differentiated epithelial cells, particularly goblet and tuft cells, while stem and transit-amplifying cells exhibited relative resistance. This differential susceptibility was strongly associated with cell type-specific expression of host entry and trafficking factors, including aminopeptidase N (APN), TMPRSS2, and Niemann-Pick C1 (NPC1). Importantly, our organoid-based infection model recapitulated in vivo-relevant antiviral responses, enabling robust evaluation of therapeutic candidates and accurately reflecting the potent antiviral efficacy of GS-441524 and the neutralizing antibody 1AF10. Collectively, this study establishes a novel, scalable, and physiologically faithful feline intestinal organoid platform that provides unprecedented insight into type II FIPV epithelial tropism and pathogenesis, and represents a powerful preclinical tool for accelerating the development of effective antiviral and preventive strategies against feline infectious peritonitis.

papers.title: Tracking human HSCs and MPPs in mice reveals distinct clonal dynamics and responses to pre-transplant conditioning.
papers.abstract: Blood and immune cell regeneration is sustained by hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), which form the therapeutic basis of bone marrow transplantation. While the functional hierarchy of mouse HSPC subsets is well characterized, the distinct roles of human HSPC populations remain less well defined, particularly at clonal resolution and in the context of transplantation conditioning. Here, we performed quantitative clonal tracking of purified human HSCs (hHSCs) and human MPPs (hMPPs) in NSGW41 mice across primary and secondary transplantation under no conditioning, and busulfan or irradiation conditioning. We found that hHSC clones generated more blood cells, initiated lymphoid production earlier, and exhibited more robust multilineage differentiation than hMPP clones. hHSC clones were also less sensitive to conditioning, maintaining stable lineage biases. Notably, busulfan and irradiation differentially affected the magnitude, lineage bias, and timing of hematopoietic reconstitution without altering engraftment. During secondary transplantation, hHSCs and hMPPs contributed comparably to hematopoietic reconstitution but with substantially reduced output and increased clonal diversity. Extramedullary hematopoiesis was observed in all secondary recipients. These findings advance our understanding of human hematopoiesis and provide a framework for optimizing experimental models, improving transplantation conditioning strategies, and informing the preclinical evaluation of HSC-based cell and gene therapies.

title.#text: Continuousproduction of CAR T cells from-transduced HSCs is safe and delays growth of mouse HER2tumors.

papers.abstract: Clinical trials with CAR T cells for solid tumors have suggested a number of problems, including critical autoimmune reactions caused by high-affinity CAR T cells, development of CAR T cell exhaustion, poor trafficking to tumor sites after intravenous CAR T cell injection, and high costs. To address these problems, we tested anHSC gene therapy approach, resulting inproduction of low-affinity mHER2-CAR-expressing T-cells in physiologically relevant immunocompetent mouse models with tumors derived from mouse HER2tumor cell lines, KPand B16F10. After intravenous injection of integrating helper-dependent adenovirus (HDAd) vectors expressing mHER2-CAR under T cell restricted transcriptional and miRNA control into mobilized C57BL/6-based mice andenrichment of stably transduced HSCs, we demonstrated that mHER2-CAR T cells significantly delayed tumor growth. Additional Treg depletion by systemic administration of low-dose cyclophosphamide further extended the time of tumor relapse driven by mHER2-negative cells. Despite continuous mHER2-CAR T cell production, theapproach had an excellent safety profile. Our study also revealed a number of obstacles that limit the efficacy of theapproach and have to be addressed in the future.

Liver fibrosis is a progressive and potentially life-threatening condition arising from chronic hepatic injury, characterized by the aberrant accumulation of extracellular matrix (ECM) driven by activated hepatic stellate cells (HSCs). The pathogenesis of fibrosis involves a complex, self-reinforcing interplay of biochemical signals, including TGF-β and PDGFβ, biomechanical cues such as matrix stiffening and viscoelastic remodeling, and multicellular crosstalk among hepatocytes, HSCs, immune cells, and sinusoidal endothelial cells. Despite growing mechanistic understanding of fibrotic progression and regression, the development of effective antifibrotic therapeutics has been significantly hampered by the limited translational fidelity of existing experimental models. Here, we review the current landscape of liver fibrosis models, spanning conventional two-dimensional cell culture, organ-on-a-chip platforms, organoids, and biomaterial-based systems, with a focus on HSC biology. We critically evaluate the capacity of each platform to decouple and interrogate the biochemical, biophysical, and cell-to-cell signals that govern HSC activation, ECM deposition, and fibrotic remodeling. We highlight advances in tunable hydrogel systems and decellularized ECM scaffolds that enable precise control of matrix mechanics and composition, as well as the emergence of iPSC-derived HSCs as a scalable and phenotypically relevant cell source. We identify critical gaps in the field, including the underutilization of biomaterial models for HSC studies and how integrated, multi-platform strategies can overcome the inherent limitations of any single model. Ultimately, this review aims to guide the rational design of next-generation fibrosis models that advance mechanistic discovery and improve the translational success of antifibrotic therapeutics.

title.#text: Leptin Receptorcells create a perisinusoidal niche for thrombopoiesis in the bone marrow by synthesizing CXCL14.

papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.abstract: Leptin Receptor-expressing (LepR) stromal cells in the bone marrow are a critical source of growth factors for the maintenance of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) and most restricted hematopoietic progenitors. An important unresolved question is whether they also regulate terminal differentiation in some hematopoietic cells. We found that bone marrow LepRcells promote thrombopoiesis by synthesizing the chemokine CXCL14.-expressing LepRcells extend fine processes that wrap around perisinusoidal megakaryocytes. Deletion offrom LepRcells did not significantly alter HSC function or most aspects of bone marrow hematopoiesis, including megakaryocyte generation; however, it significantly reduced the numbers of proplatelet-forming megakaryocytes in the bone marrow and platelets in the blood, as well as platelet quality. Megakaryocytes frommice expressed lower levels of genes that encode granule proteins as compared to control mice, leading to the release of platelets with fewer α-granules and defective thrombus formation/growth. CXCL14 promoted platelet formation by remodeling lipid metabolism in megakaryocytes, increasing fatty acid transporter expression and enabling megakaryocytes to take up more polyunsaturated fatty acids from circulation. A high fat diet rescued the formation of proplatelet-forming megakaryocytes and platelets, as well as platelet function, inmice. CXCL14 protein was sufficient to promote platelet formation by megakaryocytes in vitro and in vivo. LepRcells thus create a perisinusoidal niche for thrombopoiesis by producing CXCL14, which regulates lipid metabolism and terminal differentiation in megakaryocytes.

title.#text: FSTL1hepatic stellate cells secrete CCL3 to activate the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway, initiating anoikis resistance and promoting hepatocellular carcinoma progression.

papers.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) ranks among the most prevalent malignant tumors globally. Approximately 90% of HCC cases arise in the context of liver fibrosis, with hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) playing a pivotal role in the fibrogenic process. Follistatin-like protein 1 (FSTL1) is a secreted protein of interest in this study, which examines its impact on liver cancer cells and further elucidates its role in HCC by activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway to induce anoikis resistance. The findings indicate that FSTL1 is predominantly localized in HSCs within HCC tissues and exhibits upregulated expression compared to cirrhotic tissues. Experimental manipulation of FSTL1 expression, through stable overexpression or knockdown, correspondingly enhanced or inhibited the proliferation and migration capabilities of HSCs in vitro. Furthermore, HSCs with high FSTL1 expression were observed to facilitate the migration, invasion, in vivo growth, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) of HCC cells. In particular, HSCs with elevated levels of FSTL1 secrete CCL3, which interacts with the CCR5 receptor on the surface of HCC cells, thereby activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. This pathway activation inhibits anoikis in HCC cells, facilitating their migration, invasion, and growth in vivo. In a nude mouse model, HSCs with high FSTL1 expression significantly enhanced the growth of subcutaneous tumors derived from HCC cells. This was demonstrated by an increased Ki-67 positive index, elevated levels of CCL3 and CCR5 expression, increased Bcl-2 expression, and decreased Caspase-3 expression. In summary, HSCs with high FSTL1 expression inhibit anoikis in HCC cells through the CCL3-CCR5-PI3K/AKT/mTOR axis, thereby promoting tumor progression.

papers.title: A Carrier-Free, Co-assembled Nanoplatform for Synergistic Photothermal Therapy: Integrating High-Efficiency BODIPY with Heat Shock Protein Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: The simultaneous delivery of boron-dipyrromethene (BODIPY) photosensitizers and heat shock proteins (HSPs) inhibitors to tumor sites can enhance the therapeutic efficacy of photothermal therapy (PTT). Current strategies mainly rely on physical encapsulation into nanocarriers or chemical conjugation onto polymer backbones for the co-delivery of BODIPY and HSP inhibitors. However, these approaches are hampered by drug leakage, reproducibility, or synthetic polydispersity. Herein, we report a carrier-free, co-assembled, and self-delivery nanoplatform to overcome these limitations. An amphiphilic BODIPY derivative (BODIPY-OEG) was synthesized and co-assembled with HSP inhibitors quercetin (Q), yielding nanoparticles (B@Q) with high photothermal conversion efficiency. The resulting B@Q nanoparticles not only possessed favorable photothermal performance in vitro but also had been demonstrated to possess potent antitumor capabilities by inhibiting the expression of HSPs in tumor cells. In vivo, B@Q demonstrated potent antitumor activity by suppressing subcutaneous tumor growth and lung metastasis, while also eliciting a potent systemic immune response, demonstrating its excellent antitumor efficacy. This work proposes a simple and precise co-assembly strategy to construct carrier-free, multifunctional nanotherapeutics, which opens avenues for the concept of self-delivered synergistic PTT agents.

papers.title: Regulation of hepatic stellates cell activation by biomimetic fibrotic hydrogels with uniform and heterogeneous matrix stiffness.
papers.abstract: Current research on liver fibrosis predominantly relies on culture matrices with uniform stiffness, largely overlooking the pathophysiological relevance of stiffness heterogeneity-the spatially uneven stiffness distribution characteristic of fibrotic liver tissue. To address this, we engineered biomimetic fibrotic hydrogels using decellularized liver matrix from fibrotic tissues and methacrylated hyaluronic acid. These hydrogels replicated the distinct stiffness profiles of normal, early-stage fibrotic, and late-stage fibrotic liver. Using a custom honeycomb-shaped mold, we integrated them into a unified platform featuring both uniform and heterogeneous mechanical regions. By co-culturing hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) on this platform, we investigated how matrix stiffness regulates HSCs proliferation, migration, and activation. Results demonstrated that on uniformly stiff substrates, particularly those mimicking late-stage fibrosis, extracellular matrix components and high stiffness promoted HSCs activation, upregulated the Piezo1-YAP signaling axis. In contrast, although the low-stiffness region of the mechanically heterogeneous platform exhibited increased HSC proliferation and activation, the proliferation and activation levels in the medium- and high-stiffness regions were significantly reduced. The expression patterns of the Piezo1-YAP signaling pathway further corroborated this phenomenon. These findings suggest that mechanical heterogeneity may exert a negative regulatory effect on HSC activation. This study provides new insights into the mechanobiological mechanisms underlying hepatic fibrosis and reveals potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Bcl11a preserves hematopoietic stem cell function in culture by restraining Ncf1-dependent ROS.
papers.abstract: Ex vivo expansion of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) is limited by culture-induced oxidative stress, yet the upstream transcriptional drivers remain poorly defined. Here, we show that the transcription factor Bcl11a is rapidly and persistently downregulated during HSC culture and that this decline drives functional deterioration. Bcl11a was both required and sufficient to maintain quiescence, clonogenic activity, and serially transplantable HSC function. Mechanistically, Bcl11a directly represses a Nox2 NADPH oxidase gene module, including Ncf1, encoding the p47phox organizer subunit; Ncf1 deletion reduced ROS and partially rescued the defects of Bcl11a-deficient HSCs. Rapamycin-but not the ROS scavenger N-acetylcysteine-restored Bcl11a expression, suppressed Ncf1 and ROS, and improved HSC function, identifying Bcl11a as a candidate effector linking mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 inhibition to redox control. This axis was conserved in human hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, revealing a druggable transcriptional vulnerability of cultured HSCs and a framework for improving ex vivo-expanded grafts.

papers.title: Imaging and Analyzing the Macrophages that Regulate Pathological Hematopoietic Clones in the Mouse Calvarial Bone Marrow.
papers.abstract: The bone marrow microenvironment has been shown to regulate the progression of myeloid neoplasms. Given that bone remodeling is a dynamic process that releases bone particles as danger molecules into the bone marrow space, different stages of bone turnover across marrow cavities can impose spatial heterogeneity of inflammatory responses that impact both healthy and mutant hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs). Specifically, macrophages, serving as critical members in the HSC niche, can adopt either pro-inflammatory (M1) or anti-inflammatory (M2) phenotypes based on these local signals, which results in distinct surface receptor expression and cytokine secretion. Using intravital microscopy, a murine model of Tet2 deficiency (a prevalent mutation across the spectrum of myeloid disorders), and labeling strategies to track marrow macrophages, our recent work identified compartmentalized inflammatory landscapes in the bone marrow that differentially support expansion of mutant cells. In this chapter, we describe detailed protocols to track pathological clones with respect to marrow macrophage in live mouse calvaria, and protocols of image-guided bone button isolation to analyze pro-inflammatory cytokines from the marrow cavities of interest. These protocols can also be integrated with cell isolation for single-cell transcriptomic profiling or downstream functional assessments. The labeling strategies may be applied to image macrophages in other tissue types.

papers.title: Artepillin C from Artemisia capillaris attenuates liver fibrosis by targeting NR3C2 and regulating the PPAR-γ/Smad axis.
papers.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Artemisia capillaris is a traditional Chinese medicinal herb and widely used for the treatment of jaundice, hepatitis, and other liver-related diseases. Contemporary pharmacological studies have revealed its hepatoprotective, anti-inflammatory, and anti-fibrotic activities. However, the bioactive constituents responsible for its anti-hepatic fibrotic effect remain poorly defined. Artepillin C (AC), one of the coumaric acid derivatives isolated from A. capillaris, has not yet been studied in liver fibrosis, and its mechanism of action is still unknown. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to evaluate the anti-hepatic fibrotic effects of AC in vitro and in vivo, and to elucidate its molecular target and underlying mechanism. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The anti-fibrotic activity of AC was assessed in transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1)-induced hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation models using LX-2 and JS-1 cells, and validated in a carbon tetrachloride (CCl)-induced mouse model of liver fibrosis. The expression of extracellular matrix (ECM)-related markers were analyzed by Western blot, RT-qPCR, and immunofluorescence (IF). Transcriptomic analysis, target prediction and experimental screening were introduced to identify potential molecular targets of AC. The interaction between AC and target was validated by molecular docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, which were supported by the cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) and drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS). Receptor agonist/antagonist treatment, and co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) were conducted to explore the anti-fibrotic mechanism of AC. RESULTS: AC markedly attenuated TGF-β1-induced activation of HSCs without apparent cytotoxicity and reduced the expression of ECM proteins, including fibronectin (FN) and collagen I. In CCl-induced mice, AC alleviated liver injury and reduced ECM deposition. Transcriptomic analysis combined with target

papers.title: An AGC kinase cascade regulates ROP signaling for the correct timing of pollen germination.
papers.abstract: In flowering plants, the timing of pollen germination is crucial for successful fertilization and an important trait for seed and fruit crops. Environmental factors tightly regulate pollen germination, with germination-suppressing conditions on the pollen-producing anther and germination-promoting conditions on the receiving stigma. Using genetic, biochemical, and cell biological methods, we show that this environmental sensitivity of pollen germination in Arabidopsis thaliana is regulated by a 3-PHOSPHOINOSITIDE-DEPENDENT KINASE 1 (PDK1)-AGC1.5/AGC1.7 kinase cascade. We show that PDK1 hyperphosphorylates downstream AGC1.5/7 kinases to enhance their activity. Pollen-specific phosphoproteomics identified multiple proteins involved in pollen growth whose phosphorylation is controlled by AGC1.5/7. Two germination-promoting RHO OF PLANTS GUANINE NUCLEOTIDE EXCHANGE FACTORS (ROPGEFs) are phosphorylated by AGC1.5/7 at a novel site, reducing ROPGEF plasma membrane polarization. Loss of PDK1-AGC kinase signaling resulted in precocious pollen germination on the anther, which was rescued by high AGC1.5 kinase activity. Conversely, AGC1.5/7 overexpression or a phosphomimic ROPGEF version inhibited precocious pollen germination. Distinct subcellular localization of PDK1 and AGC1 kinases upon pollen germination is likely to alleviate their inhibitory effect. Our data indicate that the correct timing of pollen germination requires the fine-tuned activity of a PDK1-AGC1 kinase cascade inhibiting ROPGEFs on the anther, preventing precocious pollen germination.

papers.title: CHK1/2 as a potential therapeutic target in Neurofibromatosis type 2 schwannomas.
papers.abstract: The Merlin protein, encoded by the tumor suppressor gene Neurofibromatosis type II (NF2), serves as a linker between the actin cytoskeleton, the plasma membrane receptors, and other intracellular signaling molecules. While there is a basic understanding of how Merlin regulates oncogenic signaling pathways, current targeted therapies have yet to demonstrate consistent clinical efficacy. Using a library of protein kinase inhibitors, we found that NF2-null Schwann cells (SCs) were uniquely sensitive to prexasertib, a drug that targets the DNA damage response pathway kinases CHK1/2 (Checkpoint Kinase 1 and 2). NF2-null SC proliferation was also sensitive to small molecule inhibitors of CHK1/2 downstream effectors. At baseline, NF2-null SCs have increased RAC1 activity, elevated levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, and higher levels of DNA damage. Exposing NF2-null SCs to DNA damaging agents such as doxorubicin or carboplatin, alone or in combination with prexasertib, further decreased their proliferation. Consistent with this idea, suppressing RAC1 or NOX2 activity with small molecule inhibitors, decreased ROS production and restored resistance to prexasertib in NF2-null hSCs, suggesting that active RAC1 and high ROS render NF2-null hSC uniquely vulnerable to DNA damage. Furthermore, restoring NF2 expression in NF2-null Schwann cells restored their resistance to prexasertib, reduced RAC1 activity, and lowered levels of ROS and DNA damage. The intrinsic elevation of RAC1, ROS, and DNA damage in NF2-null hSCs suggest that inhibiting DNA damage response pathways might be clinically useful in patients with NF2-null schwannomas.

papers.title: Context-dependent protective and pathogenic functions of YTHDF1 in MASLD and hepatocellular carcinoma: Mechanisms and design of therapeutics.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most common chronic liver disease and can progressively develop into inflammatory metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and liver fibrosis. During this progression, activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) leads to excessive accumulation of extracellular matrix. There is a growing trend to develop into hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) for MASLD. The limited availability of effective therapeutics highlights the need to better understand the underlying pathogenic mechanisms. N6-methyladenosine (m6A) is a key post-transcriptional RNA modification that regulates gene expression and governs a broad range of physiological and pathological processes. YTH domain family 1 (YTHDF1) is a reader protein that recognizes m6A modifications on mRNAs and enhances their stability or translation by interacting with key components of the translation machinery. YTHDF1 exhibits context-dependent functions in MASLD and liver fibrosis, while it promotes HCC pathogenesis. Hepatocytic YTHDF1 alleviates MASLD by improving mitochondrial function, serving as a protective factor during its early stages. YTHDF1 in HSCs is important for initiating liver fibrosis, yet it also plays a crucial role in regulating HSC ferroptosis to counteract established fibrosis. Our structure-based analyses of YTHDF1 inhibitors reveal novel concepts, including inhibition of YTHDF1-induced condensates and direct degradation of YTHDF1 proteins by fullerene derivatives and metal-organic frameworks. YTHDF1 inhibitors serve as selective chemical probes for interrogating YTHDF1's cell type-specific functions in MASLD. They are also promising candidates for in vivo evaluation to treat MASLD and HCC and to prevent liver fibrosis at early stages.

papers.title: Megakaryopoiesis and its dysregulation in paediatric acute megakaryoblastic leukaemia.
papers.abstract: Megakaryocytes (Mks) are haematopoietic cells responsible for platelet production. They arise from haematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) through a differentiation process known as megakaryopoiesis, which is classically viewed as occurring in a stepwise manner. However, recent studies have challenged this model, suggesting an alternative direct differentiation route producing functionally distinct Mk subtypes. Understanding this process is important, as dysregulation can lead to the development of diseases such as paediatric acute megakaryoblastic leukaemia (AMKL). This is a rare subtype of acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) that has a significantly worse prognosis compared to other AML subtypes. Accurate classification of AML increasingly relies on an integrated genetic and immunophenotypic diagnostic pathway. The poor prognosis of AML is largely driven by the presence of therapy-resistant leukaemia stem cells (LSCs). Furthermore, LSCs are often resistant to targeted therapies like the BCL-2 inhibitor venetoclax, yet they show a distinct dependency on other proteins within the same apoptosis pathway, notably BCL-XL. Therefore, this review aims to summarise current knowledge on normal megakaryopoiesis and explore how its dysregulation contributes to LSC emergence in paediatric AMKL, while also highlighting the therapeutic implications of both BCL-XL dependency and emerging subtype-specific therapies.

papers.title: Epigallocatechin gallate and thermal cycling‑stimulation synergistically promote apoptosis in A549 cells via endoplasmic reticulum stress‑induced calcium ion dysregulation and oxidative stress.
papers.abstract: Non‑small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), as the predominant subtype of lung cancer, presents a considerable clinical challenge due to its high rates of recurrence and the significant adverse effects associated with conventional therapeutic modalities. In response to these challenges, the present study has explored the combined anticancer effects of epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) together with thermal cycling‑stimulation (TCS). The findings obtained demonstrated that the combination of EGCG and TCS led to a synergistic decrease in the viability of A549 and NCI‑H460 NSCLC cells, whereas IMR‑90 normal lung fibroblasts exhibited minimal cytotoxic effects. Further investigations revealed that EGCG could mitigate the TCS‑induced upregulation of the heat shock proteins (HSPs) HSP70 and HSP105, whereas the expression levels of proteasome subunits were concurrently decreased. These alterations were accompanied by the disruption of proteostasis, and also by the activation of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress‑associated pathways. Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition studies suggested a mutual interplay between inositol 1,4,5‑trisphosphate receptor‑mediated ER Ca2+ release and an excessive production of reactive oxygen species, ultimately causing the cells to undergo mitochondrial apoptosis. In summary, the present study has shown that the combined treatment of EGCG and TCS reduces the required dosage of EGCG, while also attenuating TCS‑induced heat shock responses. Consequently, the present study offers a novel and promisingproof‑of‑concept strategy for treating NSCLC.

papers.title: Redox-metabolic cascade NIR-II prodrug for synchronizing compensatory HSPs/P-gp feedback with mitophagy flux impairment against intrinsic thermotolerance.
papers.abstract: The intrinsic proteostasis of HSPs/P-gp remains formidable barriers in the multidrug resistance (MDR) and thermotolerance. To dismantle the compensatory HSPs and P-gp defense axis, we developed a metabolic reprogramming NIR-II nanoprodrug Lipid 2-DG@Au/DOX-ss, using gold liposome-nanorod loaded disulfide-doxorubicin prodrug DOX-ss and 2-deoxy-d-glucose (2-DG). Results revealed 2-DG dose-dependent metabolic perturbations of ATP, glucose, NAD, LDH. Coupled with a 24.01-fold ROS enhancement, a 5.05-fold PINK1 surge, a 0.65-fold LC3-II accumulation, 0.29-fold p62 increase, S-phase arrest (up to 64%), intensive mitophagy flux impairment was initiated to terminal cell death via NF-κB/PINK1/LC3-II pathway. Proteomic analysis further elucidates the concurrent inhibition of HSP70 (A12A)/90/B1(27)-mediated protein folding with P-gp efflux pump downregulation and the disruption of mitochondrial autophagic clearance, as well as unveiling the potent in immune modulation, ferroptosis, and calcium homeostasis. This bioenergetics-derived nanoprodrug with HSPs/P-gp compensation and mitophagy impairment provides a precise approach for eradicating recalcitrant MDR malignancies.

papers.title: High multisystem stress response is concordant with perceived arousal and predicts future depressive symptoms in the Tracking Adolescents' Individual Lives Survey.
papers.abstract: Depressive disorders increase in prevalence during adolescence and profoundly impact psychosocial functioning and quality of life. Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) and family history of depression may increase the risk for depressive disorders through altered physiological stress response. In a sample of 508 participants without prior depressive symptoms from the Tracking Adolescents' Individual Lives Survey (42% female, 58% male sex-assigned-at-birth; mean age = 16.05, SD = 0.56), we investigated longitudinal relationships between ACEs, family history, psychophysiological response to a standardized psychosocial stressor, and subsequent depressive symptoms. Latent profile analysis was used to identify stress response patterns across the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, autonomic nervous system, and perceived arousal. With generalized linear mixed modelling, we tested whether associations between ACEs and family history, and future depression varied by group. We identified four stress response patterns: low response, autonomic-reciprocal response, autonomic-coactivated response, and HPA-dominant response. Perceived arousal was concordant with physiological stress, indicating that the Self-Assessment Manikin could provide a useful proxy of stress response when physiological assessment is not feasible. Adolescents with heightened HPA response and autonomic coactivation had significantly higher future depressive symptoms compared with adolescents with autonomic reciprocity, suggesting that higher environmental sensitivity and lack of response coordination may be vulnerability factors for depressive symptoms. However, associations between ACEs, family history, and future depressive symptoms did not vary across stress response profiles. Limitations include single-time-point assessment of dynamic stress response systems and low power to detect moderation effects. Future studies could employ repeatable paradigms to capture how stress response systems develop and imp

papers.title: Exemestane induces a reduction in hematopoietic stem cells and immunotoxicity in zebrafish larvae by downregulating wnt signaling pathway.
papers.abstract: Exemestane is a third-generation aromatase inhibitor commonly prescribed for estrogen-dependent breast cancer. Given the widespread clinical use of exemestane, various adverse reactions have been reported. However, there are only a limited number of reports on the effects on the immune system. Therefore, it is essential to examine its potential toxicity and mechanism of action. In this research, zebrafish were employed as a model organism to examine the impact of exemestane on embryonic development and immune function. The larvae that were fertilized 8 h post-fertilization (hpf) were respectively exposed to exemestane solutions of different concentrations (0.9, 1.8 and 2.7 mg/L).The results demonstrated that exemestane exposure induced a concentration-dependent reduction in larval body length and an increase in yolk sac area, indicative of developmental toxicity. Subsequently, exemestane was administered to the corresponding transgenic fish lines, and it was observed that the numbers of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs), neutrophils, macrophages, and thymic T cells exhibited dose dependent decreases during exposure. Concurrently, exemestane-exposed zebrafish exhibited significantly elevated oxidative stress levels and an increased incidence of apoptotic cells. Gene expression analysis demonstrated that the immune-related gene NF-kB was downregulated, whereas tlr2 and tlr3 were upregulated in response to treatment. Notably, no significant alterations were observed in the expression levels of il-1b, prl, or lakros. . The use of astaxanthin (AS) and the wnt signaling pathway activator BML-284 can alleviate the embryonic immunotoxicity caused by exemestane. In conclusion, our study represents the first comprehensive evaluation of the immunomodulatory effects of exemestane on zebrafish larvae. These effects are likely associated with exemestane-induced elevation of oxidative stress and suppression of the Wnt signaling pathway.

papers.title: Acaudiolide attenuates MASH-related liver fibrosis through covalent engagement of SMAD4 and blockade of p-SMAD2/3 nuclear translocation.
papers.abstract: Hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation is a central driver of fibrosis progression in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), yet effective antifibrotic pharmacotherapies remain limited. Here, we identify acaudiolide, a sulfur-bridged symmetric dimeric macrodiolide isolated from the fungus Acaulium sp. H-JQSF, as a natural-product lead that suppresses HSC activation and experimental liver fibrosis. In a Western diet (WD)/CClmurine model of MASH, acaudiolide reduced collagen deposition, alpha-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA) expression and fibrogenic gene expression. Transcriptomic profiling of HSCs showed that acaudiolide antagonized transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1)-driven profibrotic programs. Mechanistically, acaudiolide did not measurably alter SMAD2/3 phosphorylation but markedly reduced the nuclear accumulation of phosphorylated SMAD2/3 (p-SMAD2/3). Integration of Connectivity Map (CMap) analysis with isotopic tandem orthogonal proteolysis-activity-based protein profiling (isoTOP-ABPP) chemical proteomics nominated SMAD4 as a candidate covalent target of acaudiolide. Covalent docking suggested Cys363 as a potential engagement site, and co-immunoprecipitation showed that acaudiolide weakened the association of SMAD4 with p-SMAD2/3. These findings support a model in which acaudiolide interferes with SMAD complex assembly, thereby attenuating TGF-β-dependent profibrotic transcription and HSC activation. Collectively, our data nominate acaudiolide as a preclinical antifibrotic lead and SMAD4 as a potentially tractable downstream node for pharmacological modulation of TGF-β signaling in MASH-related fibrosis.

papers.title: Interactive effect of childhood adversity and HPA-axis multilocus genetic variation on alexithymia in adolescents.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Childhood adversity increases risk for affective symptoms, including alexithymia, a transdiagnostic emotion-processing difficulty common in adolescence. Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis-related genetic variation may contribute to individual differences in sensitivity to adverse environments. This study examined whether an HPA-axis-related multilocus genetic profile score (MGPS) moderated the association between childhood adversity and adolescent alexithymia. METHODS: The present study addressed this issue in a sample of 460 adolescents (Mage = 12.73, SD = 0.72; 54.1% female) who completed the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire and the Toronto Alexithymia Scale. Saliva samples were collected for deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) genotyping, and an HPA-axis-related multilocus genetic profile score (MGPS) was constructed from six candidate polymorphisms. Hierarchical regression and re-parameterized regression analyses were conducted. RESULTS: Childhood adversity was positively associated with alexithymia. HPA-axis MGPS moderated this association. Specifically, adolescents with high HPA-axis MGPS exhibited higher levels of alexithymia when exposed to high childhood adversity but lower levels when exposed to low childhood adversity, providing preliminary support for the differential susceptibility model. LIMITATIONS: The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, and the findings require replication in longitudinal, clinically enriched, and more diverse samples. CONCLUSIONS: HPA-axis multilocus genetic variation may function as a biological sensitivity factor in the association between childhood adversity and adolescent alexithymia. These findings extend gene-environment interaction research to alexithymia and highlight individual differences in adolescents' emotional responses to adversity.

papers.title: Environmental sensitivity and perceived social support in relation to adolescent eating disorder symptoms.
papers.abstract: Eating disorders (EDs) frequently emerge during adolescence and are influenced by both individual and contextual factors. Among these, perceived social support has generally been associated with better outcomes, although findings remain inconsistent and may depend on both the source of support and individual differences in responsiveness to environmental inputs. The present study examined the role of Environmental Sensitivity (ES) and perceived social support in adolescent ED symptoms, focusing on different sources of support and their potential interaction within a vantage sensitivity framework. A sample of 466 adolescents (51.61% female; M = 14.80) completed self-report measures of ED symptoms, ES, and perceived social support. At a bivariate level, higher perceived support from family, teachers, friends, and peers was associated with lower ED symptoms. In covariate-adjusted models, only teachers' and family's support remained a significant predictor, while peer-related sources were no longer associated with ED symptoms. ES was consistently and positively associated with ED symptoms. Contrary to hypotheses, ES did not moderate the association between overall perceived social support and ED symptoms. Exploratory analyses suggested a sex-specific pattern, whereby the association between perceived social support and ED symptoms appeared to vary as a function of ES among males, but not females. These findings suggest that the association between social support and adolescent ED symptoms may depend on its source. Moreover, ES was consistently associated with ED symptoms. Exploratory analyses revealed that evidence for differential responsiveness to supportive contexts may vary by ES among males.

papers.title: Five-in-One NIR-II phototheranostic nanomedicine for glioblastoma multiforme: Unlocking bio-barriers and photothermal-ferroptotic amplification.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) remains a formidable therapeutic challenge due to its aggressive behavior, complex biological barriers, and high recurrence rates. Near-infrared II (NIR-II) phototheranostic nanomedicine has emerged as a promising strategy, offering deeper tissue penetration and enhanced photothermal effects for GBM treatment. Herein, we demonstrate an effective molecular design strategy that leverages expanded free space within aggregates to boost non-radiative decay and improve photothermal conversion efficiency (PCE). Based on this approach, we create a nanomedicine using holo-transferrin (holo-Tf) to encapsulate optimized phototheranostic agents (NDA-18). This nanosystem achieves efficient blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration via transferrin receptor (TfR)-mediated transcytosis and selective tumor accumulation. Upon 808 nm laser irradiation, the nanomedicine enables precise photothermal therapy (PTT) while concurrently triggering ferroptosis. This ferroptosis process further enhances the PTT efficacy by suppressing heat shock proteins (HSPs), resulting in an enhanced synergistic antitumor effect. Remarkably, this one-step self-assembled nanomedicine integrates five critical functions: from BBB penetration and tumor targeting to dual-mode imaging and synergistic PTT-ferroptosis therapy. In conclusion, we have successfully developed an innovative nanoplatform that unites rational molecular design, bioengineering, and synergistic therapy for GBM treatment.

papers.title: Role of sirtuin 7 (SIRT7) in hepatic physiology and pathophysiology: mechanism, prospective and therapeutic potential.
papers.abstract: Sirtuin 7 (SIRT7) is member of the oxidized nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD)-dependent sirtuin family of proteins that participate in the regulation of a broad spectrum of biological processes and play central roles in cellular homeostasis. Compared with other sirtuins, SIRT7 has been less studied but has emerged as an interesting regulator of chromatin stability, stress adaptation, and immune responses. In particular, emerging evidence indicates that SIRT7 participates in the regulation of endoplasmic reticulum stress (ER) , lipid metabolism, and mitochondrial function in the liver, all of which are crucial in mediating the development and progression of liver steatosis, alcoholic liver injury, hepatic fibrosis, as well as liver cancer. More importantly, genetic restoration of hepatic SIRT7 or interventions that enhance SIRT7-associated pathways have reduced hepatic steatosis and oxidative liver injury in experimental models. Related approaches have also attenuated hepatocyte apoptosis and fibrosis and reduced hepatic ferroptosis in diabetic mice. Pharmacological inhibition of SIRT7 has attenuated myeloid-driven alcoholic liver injury, promoted the clearance of activated hepatic stellate cells (HSCs), and suppressed the growth and treatment resistance of liver cancer. Collectively, these findings identify SIRT7 as a promising preclinical target for mechanistic and therapeutic investigation in liver diseases. However, current evidence is derived predominantly from cellular and animal models, and direct clinical validation remains lacking. Moreover, no selective SIRT7 activator has yet been validated in liver disease. This review summarizes the current understanding of SIRT7 structure, enzymatic properties, molecular targets, and biological functions, with particular emphasis on its roles in hepatic homeostasis and liver disease progression, and discusses the opportunities and current limitations of SIRT7 as a potential preclinical therapeutic target.

papers.title: Xiaoyao San restores NK cell anti-fibrotic activity through regulation of EZH2 in liver fibrosis.
papers.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Liver fibrosis poses a major global health issue, with few effective treatments currently available. Natural killer (NK) cells possess the capability to target activated hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) via their activating receptors, such as natural killer group 2 member D (NKG2D) and natural killer p46. Nonetheless, the fibrotic environment often limits their effectiveness in tackling fibrosis. Although the functions of Enhancer of zeste homolog 2 (EZH2) in the activation of HSCs and the regulation of NK cells are established, its influence on NK cell-driven anti-fibrotic activities in liver fibrosis, along with the mechanisms by which the traditional Chinese remedy Xiaoyao San (XYS) demonstrates its anti-fibrotic properties, remain to be fully clarified. PURPOSE: This study aims to investigate whether EZH2 suppresses NK cell anti-fibrotic function by reducing NK cell abundance, maturation, and activation, and to evaluate whether XYS restores NK cell-mediated elimination of activated HSCs through EZH2 inhibition. METHODS: We established carbon tetrachloride-induced liver fibrosis in mice with NK cell-specific conditional knockout of Ezh2 and mice with hepatocyte-specific overexpression of Ezh2 with or without XYS intervention. In vitro co-culture experiments using LX-2 and NK92MI cells were performed to dissect direct effects of XYS on EZH2 expression and NK cell cytotoxicity. Liver fibrosis was assessed by histology, serum biochemistry, and Western blot. NK cell abundance, maturation, and NKG2D expression were examined through flow cytometry. Both bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing were conducted to characterize transcriptomic alterations. RESULTS: NK cell-specific deletion of Ezh2 attenuated carbon tetrachloride-induced fibrosis, increased hepatic NK cell proportion and the abundance of mature CD11b⁺ NK subsets, and altered NK cell effector gene expression. Conversely, hepatocyte-specific overexpression of Ezh2 exacerbated fibrosis, reduced NK c

papers.title: Parental support moderates the interaction of COMT and BDNF genotypes with early life adversity on problem gambling severity index scores among young adults.
papers.abstract: The development of gambling-related harm and gambling disorder involves several genetic and environmental factors. However, how these factors interact to influence the development and whether such interactions confer to diathesis-stress or differential susceptibility models remains largely unexplored. To address this gap, data from the Survey of Adolescent Life in Västmanland (SALVe cohort) were utilized, Participants provided a saliva sample for genotyping, completed early life adversity (ELA) and Parents as Social Construct (PASCQ) surveys at age 17, and the Problem Gambling Severity Index (PGSI) at age 23. A total of 391 participants (54% females) with complete data were included for analysis. Negative binomial models were utilized to examine the interaction between candidate genes (COMT, BDNF, and DRD2), ELA, and parental support in PGSI scores. Interactions between COMT and BDNF, ELA, and parental support were found but not for DRD2, (β = -0.01 and -0.009, 95% CI [-0.02, -0.006 and -0.01, -0.005], p = 2.2 × 10and 1.2 × 10respectively). The interactions remained significant after accounting for sex interactions, p = 0.005. Notably, evidence for a differential susceptibility framework was found in gambling-related harm scores. Participants with the major allele for both COMT and BDNF displayed plasticity by exhibiting higher PGSI scores when exposed to weak parental support but lower PGSI scores in strong parental support despite higher ELA scores. Positive parental support acted as a protective factor against the genetic sensitivity of gambling-related harm. Studies pursuing the interplay between genetic and environmental factors would benefit from including positive environments that may mitigate the risk associated with adverse environments.

papers.title: Structure-guided mapping of ototoxicity-related proteins: drug entry, damage amplification, cell death execution, and endogenous otoprotection.
papers.abstract: Drug-induced ototoxicity remains a clinically relevant challenge associated with the use of several essential pharmacological agents, because effective strategies to prevent permanent auditory or vestibular damage are still limited. Ototoxic drugs differ in their chemical structure, therapeutic indication, and mechanism of action, but their damaging effects converge on partially overlapping molecular events within cochlear and vestibular tissues. These events include drug access to inner-ear compartments and cellular uptake, calcium dysregulation, oxidative stress, inflammatory amplification, mitochondrial dysfunction, apoptotic execution, and the failure or insufficiency of endogenous protective responses. In this review, we organize ototoxicity-related proteins into four interconnected functional layers: drug access and entry pathways, intracellular stress amplification and damage mediation, cell death execution, and endogenous otoprotective and repair-oriented responses. For each layer, we discuss proteins with functional relevance in the inner ear, available structural information, known ligands, binding-site data, and therapeutic tractability. This structure-guided perspective highlights early entry checkpoints such as TMC1/TMC2, OCT2, CTR1, and TRPV1; damage-amplifying hubs such as NOX3, inflammatory signaling mediators, RGS17, PRMTs, and CDK2; execution mediators such as Bax, calpains, and caspases; and protective systems including HSPs, G6PD, BDNF, PINK1, KCNQ4, and sirtuins. We propose that effective otoprotection will require precise modulation rather than simple inhibition of these targets. Finally, we discuss structural druggability, delivery challenges, timing of intervention, model limitations, and target prioritization as key considerations for the rational development of precision otoprotective strategies.

papers.title: Universal single-copy genes and 16S rDNA present incongruent evolutionary histories in Vibrio.
papers.abstract: A common technique for the study of the diversity and evolution of microbial communities is 16S rDNA sequencing. However, high sequence identity and variable copy number constrain the application of 16S rDNA in differentiation of closely related taxa and estimation of species relative abundance in environmental samples. A promising alternative is the use of universal single-copy genes as phylogenetic markers. We explore this alternative by analyzing a set of single-copy loci from the genus Vibrio, which comprises more than 100 species of substantial ecological and epidemiological relevance. The phylogenetic histories of these loci, of representative copies of 16S and 23S rDNA genes, and of a collection of partial 16S rDNA sequences were reconstructed using Bayesian inference. Taxon resolution was assessed according to consensus tree topology and clade credibility values. In addition, the congruence among posterior distributions of phylogenetic estimates of the different loci was calculated using Robinson-Foulds distances and visualized with non-metric multidimensional scaling. Phylogenetic analyses reveal that Vibrio single-copy loci produce highly resolved trees in comparison to those of 16S and 23S rDNA sequences. We also observe relatively high congruence among phylogenies of Vibrio single-copy loci while rDNA phylogenies diverge from these. The loci mfd and uvrC are highlighted for further research on Vibrio evolution and analysis of environmental samples. Moreover, possible sources of phylogenetic incongruence between Vibrio single-copy and rDNA loci include differential susceptibility to horizontal gene transfer, as potentially explained by the complexity hypothesis, or lack of phylogenetic information due to limited sequence variability in rDNA sequences.

papers.title: Enhancing the Functionality of Human Bone Marrow-Derived Mesenchymal Stromal Cells Using Signaling Modulators.
papers.abstract: Bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (BM-MSCs) possess an inherent capacity to support hematopoiesis in vitro. As a result, they are often used as feeder layers for the ex vivo expansion of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) or coinfused with HSCs to improve the success of clinical transplants. However, MSCs isolated from non-hematopoietic tissues such as adipose or dental tissue may not be as effective as BM-MSCs in supporting hematopoiesis. Additionally, BM-MSCs tend to lose their functional ability after extended in vitro culture, which is necessary for producing sufficient cell numbers for clinical use. These limitations underscore the importance of pretreating MSCs with suitable signaling modulators to boost their functionality. Reliable in vitro assays play a crucial role in finding such signaling compounds and evaluating their effects on MSCs. Conventional assays, such as long-term-culture-initiating assay (LTC-IC assay) or colony-forming-unit assay (CFU assay), chemotactic migration assays (e.g., Transwell assay), etc., primarily evaluate the functional competence of HSCs and HSPCs, but provide little insight into the hematopoiesis-supportive capacity of MSCs. This chapter describes two such assays: one is designed to assess the hematopoietic stem/progenitor cell (HSPC)-supporting capacity of primed MSCs, and the other is specifically aimed at their ability to support the growth of primitive HSCs. These assays can serve as initial screens to test the impact, whether positive or negative, synergistic or antagonistic, of known signaling compounds, bioactive peptides, growth factors, and cytokines on MSC function or to discover new entities that could boost the functionality of MSCs.

title.#text: FeN@C nanomaterials: Synergistic PTT/CDT/NO for the dynamic therapy of diabetic foot ulcer.

papers.abstract: Diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) is one of the most severe complications of diabetes, and its multiple pathological factors render treatment more challenging. We synthesized FeN@C nanomaterials to integrate synergistic photothermal therapy/chemical dynamic therapy/nitric oxide (PTT/CDT/NO) for DFU therapy. First, FeOand urea were used as precursors to synthesize FeN@C nanomaterials via nitridation. The nanomaterial can serve as a new NO donor that releases NO triggered by Hand reactive oxygen species (HOand O). Furthermore, FeN@C possess superhigh peroxidase (POD)-like activity (V = 21.1 Ms., pH 5.5), catalyzing endogenous HOinto hydroxyl radicals (OH). POD activity can also amplify NO and peroxynitrite (ONOO) production. In addition, Fe₂N@C nanomaterials reveal high near-infrared II (NIR-II) light harvest and photothermal conversion efficiency (43.94%). Hyperthermia also synergistically boosts POD-like activity and NO release. Under NIR-II laser irradiation, the combination of PTT/CDT and high NO concentration of can quickly clear bacterial infection. In addition, NO can down-regulate the expression of heat shock proteins (HSPs) to amplify PTT performance. Then, the mild NO supply (without irradiation) further facilitates the reversal of inflammation (M2 macrophage polarization) and tissue regeneration (angiogenesis). This dynamic synergistic therapy promotes fast normal DFU healing.

papers.title: PXDN knockdown alleviates hepatic stellate cell activation by regulating GPX1.
papers.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
papers.abstract: The central mechanism of cholestatic liver fibrosis (CLF) is the accumulation of extracellular matrix caused by the activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs), which is reversible in the early to mid-stages. Therefore, this study characterized the underlying molecular mechanisms involved. In this study, the liver and spleen indexes of the CLF model markedly increased and continued to rise over time. There were significant differences in ALP, TBIL, AST, DBIL, ALT, IBIL, AST/ALT, and GGT levels among rats in the CLF and SHAM groups at different time points. Histological staining revealed that the CLF had progressed to cirrhosis by week 5. Importantly, relative to the SHAM group, the CLF-2, CLF-3, CLF-4, and CLF-5 groups contained 2886, 3472, 5297, and 4586 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), respectively. The four comparisons identified 1848 shared DEGs that regulate cell growth, chemotaxis, inflammation, apoptosis, and fibrosis. Pxdn and Gpx1 are the hub genes for these shared DEGs. Pxdn knockdown reversed the TGF-β-induced increase in HSC activity and markers (Col I, α-SMA, and FN), an effect that was rescued by Gpx1 knockdown. Pxdn knockdown increased GPX1 levels in HSCs, whereas Gpx1 knockdown had no effect on PXDN. In conclusion, Pxdn knockdown attenuated TGF-β-induced activation of HSC by upregulating GPX1. These findings nominate the PXDN-GPX1 axis as a mechanistic candidate warranting in vivo interrogation.

papers.title: Attenuation of liver fibrosis by platelet-type 12S-lipoxygenase expressed in hepatic stellate cells involves repression of platelet-derived growth factor receptors.
papers.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular and cell biology of lipids
papers.abstract: Progression of liver fibrosis is a critical determinant of the prognosis of chronic inflammatory liver disease. We previously reported that platelet-type 12S-lipoxygenase localized in hepatic stellate cells (HSCs), which are primary fibrogenic cells in the injured liver, was upregulated in a methionine-choline deficiency (MCD) diet-induced mouse liver fibrosis model. In this study, the functional contribution of platelet-type 12S-lipoxygenase to the pathological process was investigated. After feeding with an MCD diet for 8 weeks, platelet-type 12S-lipoxygenase-deficient (Alox12) mice exhibited significantly greater Sirius Red-positive areas and higher expression of type I collagen genes (Col1a1 and Col1a2) than wild-type (WT) mice, indicating aggravated fibrosis. Similar results were obtained in a model induced by neonatal streptozotocin injection followed by a high-fat diet (HFD) feeding. Conversely, a human HSC line (TWNT-1) stably overexpressing human platelet-type 12S-lipoxygenase exhibited significantly reduced COL1A1 and COL1A2 expression compared to the parental and mock cells. Analysis of fibrosis-related genes revealed downregulation of platelet-derived growth factor receptors (PDGFR) α and β in platelet-type 12S-lipoxygenase-expressing TWNT-1 cells. Consistently, the hepatic expression of Pdgfra and Pdgfrb was significantly elevated in MCD diet-fed Alox12mice compared to that in MCD diet-fed WT mice. The knockdown of PDGFRs in parental TWNT-1 cells using siRNAs significantly suppressed the expression of type I collagen genes. Collectively, these findings indicate that platelet-type 12S-lipoxygenase expressed in HSCs attenuates liver fibrosis, at least in part, by modulating PDGFR expression.

papers.title: Associations of sensory processing sensitivity with cannabis motives and consumption in young adults.
papers.abstract: Sensory processing sensitivity (SPS) is a personality trait characterized by heightened responsiveness to both internal and environmental stimuli. Because substances can be used to reduce overstimulation, it has been hypothesized that SPS may correlate to cannabis use. Limited research has examined these associations, finding no relationship with cannabis abuse. Beyond levels of use, SPS could be associated with motives for using cannabis, but this has yet to be examined. The present study examined concurrent associations of SPS with cannabis use frequency, cannabis abuse symptoms, and cannabis use motives in young adults. Participants were 195 23-year-olds from Québec, Canada who self-reported SPS and cannabis measures. Path analyses indicated that SPS was not related to cannabis use frequency or abuse symptoms. Further, SPS was related to social, coping, and expansion motives for cannabis use. When examining SPS subscales, low sensory threshold/ease of excitation was associated with social and conformity motives for cannabis use, while aesthetic sensitivity was associated with enhancement and expansion motives. These results suggest that SPS is related to diverse cannabis motives, rather than only to coping as hypothesized in previous literature. Motivations for cannabis use could inform intervention strategies that are implemented when individuals high in SPS seek treatment for cannabis use problems.
